question: In the morning, a fishing charter boat catches 56 fish. By midday, a lucky second run triples the boat's catch. In the early afternoon, 3 more fish are caught by a passenger using his own rod. The boat's captain, Hollis, mentions a rival charter only caught 40 fish today, far behind this boat's haul. By late afternoon, a final deep-water run brings the catch to 5 times what it had grown to. That evening, a last group of anglers brings the total catch to 3 times what it was. How many fish did the boat catch by the end of the day?

A charity clothing drive has 236 jackets collected at the start of winter. A local business donates 27 more jackets. A dozen churches held a joint collection event that same week, though that number has nothing to do with the jacket count. A radio station's donation push brings the jacket count to 5 times what it was. A distribution event to shelters gives out 568 jackets. A final small donation adds 3 more jackets. The remaining jackets are then split evenly across 5 shelters, and the story follows just one shelter's share. How many jackets does that one shelter have?

In the morning, a food pantry has 109 cans of soup on its shelves. By midday, a donation adds 13 more cans. In the early afternoon, a huge community food drive brings the shelves' count to 6 times what it was. By late afternoon, the pantry director gives away exactly half of the cans to a partner shelter across town, keeping the rest on the shelves. That evening, 74 more cans arrive from a grocery store's surplus. Right before closing, 48 final cans are added from a last-minute donation box. How many cans of soup are on the shelves now?

Maria kept track of the total messages in her phone's inbox throughout the week, starting with 96 unread messages. She deleted 82 of them after a big cleanup. Later, 55 new messages arrived from her book club, and then 16 more came in from a work channel. By the end of the week, an automated forwarding rule tripled the number of messages sitting in her inbox. How many unread messages were in Maria's inbox by the end of the week?

A charity book fair had 209 books on the tables when doors opened. A visitor mentioned there were 15 volunteers helping out that day, though that had nothing to do with the book count. During the morning rush, organizers added 70 more donated books to the tables. By midday, families had taken home 120 books total. In the afternoon, a school delivered 21 more books to the tables. That evening, a local library multiplied the remaining book count by 9 to estimate how many books would be needed for a citywide donation drive. A dozen posters were also put up to advertise the fair. How many books did the citywide estimate come to?

A charity raffle sold 90 tickets before the fair began. During setup, organizers voided 23 tickets that were duplicates. They also set aside 8 tickets for staff prizes, no longer counting them in the live total. A radio sponsor then said the promotion would triple the number of tickets still in play, so the live count was tripled. A late rush at the gate added 40 more valid tickets, and shortly after, a group of teachers bought 41 more. A printing error, however, meant 188 tickets had to be pulled from the live count entirely due to a batch defect. A raffle box elsewhere had 50 blank tickets that were never sold. How many tickets remained in the live count?

A classroom had 40 pencils in the supply bin on Monday. During art class, 31 pencils were used up and tossed. The remaining pencils were split evenly among 3 group bins, and the teacher tracked just one bin's count. That bin lost 2 more pencils when a student broke them. On Tuesday, a supply order added 37 pencils to that same bin. By Wednesday, a neighboring classroom borrowed 34 pencils from that bin permanently. Meanwhile, the school's main supply closet held 500 pencils in reserve, unrelated to this bin. How many pencils were left in the tracked bin?

Sam kept a running balance in his lemonade stand cash box all afternoon, starting with 67 dollars. His business partner Ellie, by comparison, ran a cookie stand with a separate box holding 40 dollars, but only Sam's box is tracked here. A customer's big order added 10 dollars to Sam's box. A syrup restock then cost him 36 dollars. A spilled pitcher led to an 18-dollar refund taken out of the box. Finally, an evening rush added 67 more dollars to Sam's box. How much money was in Sam's cash box by the end of the afternoon?

The library's mystery section began the day with 118 books checked out. A morning return dropped that number by 7. A cataloging fix then doubled the official checkout count when duplicate holds were resolved. An afternoon return event brought the count down by 65. A book club sign-up doubled the checkout count once more. A branch-wide sync multiplied that number by 9 to combine it with identical sister-branch totals. Finally, an evening rush added 67 more checkouts to the tally. For her report, the librarian converted the checkout period from two weeks into 14 days, a simple unit change unrelated to the tally. The reference section, unrelated to this tally, had 300 books checked out separately that day. How many checkouts did the combined tally show by the end of the day?

A dairy farm tracked the total liters of milk in its holding tank throughout the day, starting with 117 liters at dawn. During the morning milking, 34 liters were drawn off for the local creamery. By midmorning, a second herd's milking added 61 liters back into the tank. In the afternoon, the tank's contents were split evenly into 3 identical cooling vats, and only the first vat's amount was tracked from then on — the farmer noted this in her log as converting from tank liters to vat liters, a simple unit change. That afternoon, a delivery from a neighboring farm added 67 more liters to the tracked vat. By evening, a cheese-making batch used up 80 liters from the tracked vat. How many liters were in the tracked vat by the end of the evening?

A charity tracked the total dollars raised in its online donation counter all week, starting at 83 dollars. A matching-donor program multiplied the counter by 4. A platform fee then took back a quarter of that, dividing the counter by 4 to reflect just the net amount kept — the treasurer noted this in her log as converting gross dollars to net dollars, a simple unit change. A refund request then removed 12 dollars from the net counter. A late donation added 15 more dollars. Finally, a corporate sponsor multiplied the net counter by 5. How many dollars did the net counter show by the end of the week?

A warehouse tracked its crate inventory throughout the day, starting with 127 crates at opening. During the morning shift, 61 crates were shipped out. By midmorning, another 17 crates went out on a rush order. In the afternoon, a returning shipment multiplied the remaining crate count by 5 after a supplier sent back a full truckload. A dozen forklifts were in use that afternoon, though that had nothing to do with the crate count. By late afternoon, 40 crates were pulled for a damaged-goods inspection. By evening, a merger with a sister warehouse multiplied the tracked count by 4. A separate loading dock, unrelated to this count, processed 200 crates that day. How many crates were in the tracked count by the end of the evening?

A moving company tracked the total weight of boxes loaded onto Truck 3 all day, starting at 127 pounds already loaded. A homeowner's early delivery added 76 more pounds. A recheck found 35 pounds of that had been mislabeled and removed from the truck. Another 21 pounds were taken off when a fragile box was reassigned to a different truck. Finally, the crew converted the last batch's weight from kilograms to pounds for the manifest — a simple unit change — before adding 56 more pounds to Truck 3. How many pounds were loaded onto Truck 3 by the end of the day?

A fish tank at the pet store held 15 goldfish at opening, tracked as the store's featured tank all day. A dozen customers stopped by just to look, though that number has nothing to do with the fish count. A wholesale return took 12 fish back to the supplier. A restocking delivery then doubled the number of fish in the tank. A sick fish was removed by the staff, taking one out. Later, three fish were sold to a single customer. A separate tank across the store held 40 turtles, unrelated to this count. How many goldfish were in the featured tank by the end of the day?

A movie theater tracked the number of seats reserved for Screen 5 all evening, starting with 237 seats reserved at showtime. A late group booking added 75 more reserved seats. A cancellation then freed up 36 seats. A double-booking error later required the theater to release 155 seats back to general sale. Screen 2, unrelated to this tracked count, sold 400 tickets that night. The manager also converted the film's runtime from minutes to hours for the schedule board, a simple unit change unrelated to the seat count. Finally, a last-minute group reservation added 22 more seats to Screen 5's tracked count. How many seats were reserved for Screen 5 by the end of the evening?

A toy factory produced 148 boxes of action figures in one run. Each box actually contained enough figures to fill 4 retail boxes once repackaged, multiplying the total. A shipping error then meant 405 boxes had to be pulled for relabeling. A separate quality check removed another 183 boxes for defects. A different production line, unrelated to this batch, made 700 boxes that same day. Finally, a returned shipment added 10 more boxes back to the count. How many boxes were left in this batch's count?

Coach Diaz tracked the total points scored by his basketball team across the tournament, starting with 79 points banked from an early qualifying game. His rival, Coach Reyes, had a team that had scored 500 points that season, far more overall, but this story only follows Diaz's tracked total. A blowout win multiplied Diaz's tracked total by 8. A make-up game added 79 more points. A forfeiture then subtracted 664 points due to a scoring reversal. A championship multiplier from the league then multiplied the tracked total by 9. A penalty deducted 88 points. Finally, a bonus round multiplied the tracked total by 9 once more. How many points did Coach Diaz's tracked total show at the end of the tournament?

Omar tracked the total dollars in his coin collection's estimated value, starting at 82 dollars for his current set. His cousin Yusuf, by comparison, had a collection appraised at 600 dollars, much higher than Omar's. A rare coin then multiplied Omar's collection's estimated value by 5. A market correction dropped the estimated value by 399 dollars. A new appraisal added 35 dollars back. Finally, a coin show purchase added 10 more dollars to the estimated value. How much was Omar's collection estimated to be worth?

Grace tracked the total miles she'd biked this month, starting with 155 miles logged. Her training partner, Wes, had already logged 300 miles, way more than Grace. A weekend ride added 16 more miles to Grace's total. A charity ride then added 55 more miles. A half-dozen new bike routes opened in town, though that number has nothing to do with her mileage. A commute streak added 30 more miles. Finally, a rainy week meant Grace lost the equivalent of 61 miles from her monthly goal, subtracted from her tracked total. How many miles did Grace's tracked total show?

A bacteria culture in a lab began the morning with 58 cells under the microscope. By late morning, the population multiplied sixfold under ideal conditions. By afternoon, it quadrupled again as nutrients were added. By early evening, it quadrupled once more. By late evening, a final quadrupling occurred before the lab closed. A separate control culture, unrelated to this one, started with 200 cells. How many cells were in the tracked culture by late evening?

A campground tracked the number of guests checked in throughout the day, starting with 166 guests already on-site at dawn. During the morning, 46 more guests checked in. By midday, 130 guests checked out. In the afternoon, 78 more guests arrived. By early evening, 69 guests left for a day trip and didn't return. By dusk, 15 more guests checked in. A dozen park rangers patrolled the grounds that day, though that number has nothing to do with guest count. Finally, at night, 3 more late arrivals checked in. How many guests were on-site by night?

Warehouse manager Dana tracked the total inventory units in Aisle 7 throughout the day, starting with 221 units at opening. Her counterpart, manager Felix, tracked Aisle 9 separately, which held 400 units that morning, but only Dana's aisle is followed here. During the morning, a bulk shipment out reduced Dana's tracked count by 198 units. By midday, a restock multiplied the tracked count by 6. In the afternoon, a supplier bonus multiplied the tracked count by 9 once more. By late afternoon, a small delivery added 33 more units. By evening, a final delivery added 26 more units. How many units were in Aisle 7's tracked count by evening?

Ravi tracked the total dollars in his savings account all month, starting at 110 dollars. His roommate, Tomás, had a separate account with 900 dollars, far more than Ravi's, but only Ravi's account is tracked here. A paycheck deposit added 49 dollars to Ravi's account. Rent then took out 38 dollars. Groceries took another 70 dollars. A phone bill took 39 more dollars. Finally, a bonus at work tripled whatever remained in Ravi's tracked account. How much money was in Ravi's account by the end of the month?

Landlord Priya tracked the total rent collected from her apartment building this month, starting at 176 dollars from early payments. Her business partner, Marcus, separately managed a second building that had already collected 900 dollars, but only Priya's building is tracked here. Early in the month, a batch of six tenants paid their full rent at once, multiplying the tracked total by 6. Midway through the month, a late fee added 28 dollars. Later that month, a parking fee added 13 more dollars. Near the end of the month, a laundry room payout added 55 more dollars. A dozen new tenants had moved in that year, though that number has nothing to do with this month's total. Finally, at month's end, a special assessment multiplied the tracked total by 9. How much rent did Priya's tracked total show at the end of the month?

Elena tracked the total dollars in her lemonade stand's cash box, starting with 37 dollars from yesterday's leftover. Her friend Bianca, by comparison, ran a stand that had already made 200 dollars, way more than Elena's box. A big fundraiser event multiplied Elena's tracked cash box by 9 once matching donations came in. A supply cost of 246 dollars was then paid out of the box. A customer's tip added 53 dollars. Another sale added 4 more dollars. Elena also converted her running total from dollars to cents for a raffle entry form — a simple unit change unrelated to the cash box tracked in dollars. Finally, a final sale added 64 more dollars to the box. How many dollars were in Elena's cash box by the end of the day?
